intention: Every registered vehicle carries its two static Tesla attributes (exterior_color, car_type) on the vehicles registry row, captured once per vehicle from the nightly collector's existing VehicleData call, so the registry read port serves them with no Tesla call and no cross-module access.
request: /kkpa-dev-harness-pipeline continue -> user selected the pre-existing plan doc openspec/changes/accout-vehicles-add-static-fields/proposal.md ('account - static vehicle fields'): persist exterior_color + car_type on the account vehicles registry, back-filled from the nightly telemetry collector's existing VehicleData call. Then: 'execute the openspec plan with autopilot mode'.

decisions.decision: Capture rides on the nightly telemetry collector's existing tesla.VehicleData call, not a separate one-shot job.
decisions.why: Zero extra paid Fleet API cost; the collector already fetches the payload per vehicle after the wake flow.

decisions.decision: Write trigger is a Go guard on the already-fetched OwnedVehicle (skip when both fields non-nil) PLUS an OR-semantics SQL condition: AND (exterior_color IS NULL OR car_type IS NULL).
decisions.why: Defense-in-depth. The Go guard means zero DB traffic after night 1; the SQL condition self-heals a partial row and prevents clobbering. updated_at moves only on a real write. Mirrors RM5 RD2.

decisions.decision: Field scope is exactly exterior_color + car_type. A curated 7-field display set and a full vehicle_config JSONB column were both rejected.
decisions.why: Strict YAGNI; the live payload has 47 keys but no consumer needs more than these two. Further fields are a separate change.

decisions.decision: Failure mode is best-effort AND counted: never changes Reason, never writes a poll_attempts row, retried next cycle, increments a new CycleReport.ConfigCaptureFailures surfaced in the scheduler's cycle log.
decisions.why: Mirrors the existing ChargingFetchFailures precedent in the same module; without the counter a permanently failing back-fill would be log-only and invisible.

decisions.decision: An empty string from Tesla means skip the write and leave NULL; the collector calls the port only when both observed values are non-empty.
decisions.why: Writing "" would satisfy both the Go guard and the SQL IS NULL condition, permanently marking the vehicle captured with a non-value that can never self-heal. NULL keeps 'not yet captured' literally true and retries next cycle.

decisions.decision: attemptVehicle returns (Reason, vehicleConfig) and never calls s.acct; the nil/empty guard, the SetVehicleConfigIfEmpty call and the ConfigCaptureFailures increment all live in collectAccount beside record(...).
decisions.why: Preserves both existing invariants: exactly one capture per vehicle per cycle (retry-safe, since collectVehicle may call attemptVehicle twice) and all account-port access at the level where AccessTokenFor already lives. attemptVehicle stays a pure [wake->]fetch->map->store pass.

decisions.decision: collectVehicle/attemptVehicle take v account.OwnedVehicle in place of the separate accountID + teslaID params.
decisions.why: Net parameter reduction; the nil-check sits next to the data it tests, and future registry-driven behaviour needs no further signature churn. Rejected: a needsConfig bool param (encodes a check performed elsewhere).

decisions.decision: The internal/tesla VehicleConfigTesla DTO addition is a leaf granted path inside tier 2, not a tier of its own; RM6 therefore has 2 tiers, not 3.
decisions.why: Additive ...Tesla DTO field with no new VehicleService method and no Raw*/explorer change. Follows the merged telemetry-add-tire-pressure-columns T1 precedent verbatim; a ~10-line struct addition should not pay a full tier's proposal/design/tasks/spec/review overhead.

decisions.decision: Removed the superseded plan doc folder openspec/changes/accout-vehicles-add-static-fields/ in the roadmap commit; its content is carried forward into this roadmap and the tier proposal prompts.
decisions.why: It was a planning note (proposal.md only, no design/tasks/specs, no progress.json, misspelled 'accout-'), not a validated OpenSpec change. Leaving it would leave a second, stale source of truth for the same work.
